lead: Recent advancements in robotics highlight the integration of AI and innovative training methods, showcasing the potential for robots to learn from vast amounts of data and adapt to new environments.

stories.title: They Trained Robots on 100 Million Videos. Here's What Happened
stories.summary: Rhoda AI is pioneering a novel approach to robotics by training its models on 100 million internet videos rather than traditional lab data. This innovative method allows robots to learn complex physics and behaviors from real-world scenarios captured in video format. The implications for future robotics development could be significant, as the technology aims to enhance robot adaptability and functionality.

stories.title: Agility Robotics plants its flag in Tesla’s backyard
stories.summary: Agility Robotics has announced the opening of a new training center for its Digit robots in Fremont, California, strategically located near Tesla's operations. This move signifies Agility's commitment to advancing humanoid robotics and could foster collaborations with automotive innovations. The training center is expected to enhance the capabilities of Digit, making it more efficient in performing tasks in dynamic environments.

stories.title: China creates World AI body with Russia and 27 others, but without US
stories.summary: China has established the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO) with 28 other countries, aiming to set global standards and regulations for AI, including robotics. Notably absent from this initiative are major players like the US and EU, highlighting a shift in the global AI landscape. This organization seeks to bridge the capability divide in AI development and could influence international robotics standards.
